response.evidence: These figures are approximate, from a manual review of the rows rather than an exact computation. White Male applicants show roughly 15 denials out of about 250-300 applications, a denial rate of about 5-6%. That is similar to or slightly below the overall rate in the dataset and lower than the apparent rate for Hispanic or Latino applicants. Most White Male denials have clear risk factors: debt-to-income above 50% (e.g., >60% DTI on $865K, $935K, $945K and $485K loans; 50%-60% DTI on $45K, $35K and $315K loans) or reported income of 0 ($255K and $725K loans). The same factors appear in denials across every racial and sex group. Some White Male applicants with high DTI (50%-60%) were still approved. Denials appear driven by DTI and income rather than race or sex. Limitation: this dataset lacks credit scores and other underwriting variables, so it can show no evidence of disparity but cannot fully prove the absence of discrimination.
